photos.question: A healthy adult asks about acetaminophen. What is the usual maximum daily dose?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #315!

💊 Everyone takes it, but do you know the safe daily limit?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — 4 grams

🧠 Rationale: For most healthy adults, the max is 4 grams (4,000 mg) in 24 hours.

Too much can cause severe liver damage.

Lower limits are used for liver disease or heavy alcohol use.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Acetaminophen

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Analgesic and antipyretic

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Mild pain and fever

⚠️ Overdose Signs:

🔹 Nausea and vomiting early

🔹 Right upper abdominal pain

🔹 Jaundice and rising liver enzymes later

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Check labels: many combo products contain it

✅ Do not go over the daily max

✅ Limit alcohol

🚑 Antidote:

🔹 Acetylcysteine

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

FOUR is the ceiling: never more than 4 grams in a day!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: An adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Which pulse should the nurse check?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #316!

❤️ Seconds count in a code. Where do you check the pulse?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac emergency question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Carotid pulse

🧠 Rationale: The carotid pulse is checked in adults during CPR.

It is a large central artery that stays palpable when peripheral pulses are lost.

Check for no more than 10 seconds before starting compressions.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Adult CPR Basics

❤️ Pulse Check:

🔹 Adult and child: carotid

🔹 Infant: brachial

🔹 10 seconds max

🚨 Compressions:

✅ 100 to 120 per minute

✅ At least 2 inches deep in adults

✅ Allow full chest recoil

✅ 30 compressions to 2 breaths without an advanced airway

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Call for help and an AED right away

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Carotid for the CENTER of the action: adults get the neck, infants get the arm!

photos.question: Which finding should the nurse expect in a client with long-term emphysema?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #317!

🫁 Look at the chest shape. What does long-term emphysema do?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Barrel-shaped chest

🧠 Rationale: Emphysema traps air in the lungs and causes hyperinflation.

Over time the chest widens front to back, giving a barrel shape.

Pink frothy sputum points to pulmonary edema, not emphysema.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Emphysema

🫁 What Happens:

🔹 Alveoli lose elasticity

🔹 Air gets trapped

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Barrel chest

🔹 Pursed-lip breathing

🔹 Use of accessory muscles

🔹 Thin build, tripod position

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Upright or tripod position

✅ Low-flow oxygen as ordered

✅ Small, high-calorie meals

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Emphysema = trapped air = a chest shaped like a BARREL full of air!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse teaches a client to use an insulin pen. Which step should the client do before each dose?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #318!

💉 Insulin pens look simple, but one step gets skipped all the time. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Prime the pen with 2 units

🧠 Rationale: Priming with an air shot of 2 units clears air and makes sure the needle works.

Skipping it can lead to a smaller dose than ordered.

Use a new needle every time and hold the pen in place about 10 seconds after injecting.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Insulin Pen Technique

💉 Steps:

✅ Wash hands, check the label and expiration

✅ Roll cloudy insulin gently, never shake

✅ Attach a new needle

✅ Prime 2 units until a drop appears

✅ Dial the dose and inject

✅ Hold 10 seconds, then remove

⚠️ Storage:

🔹 Unopened pens in the fridge

🔹 Never freeze

🚨 Teaching:

✅ Rotate sites

✅ Never share pens

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

PRIME before you DIAL: an air shot every time!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Insulin #Diabetes #Endocrine #PatientTeaching #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse teaches new parents about safe sleep. How should a healthy infant be placed to sleep?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #319!

👶 This simple habit saves infant lives. Do you know the rule?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric safety question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — On the back

🧠 Rationale: Healthy infants should be placed on their back for every sleep.

Back sleeping lowers the risk of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS).

Pillows, blankets and soft toys should stay out of the crib.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Infant Safe Sleep

👶 Safe Sleep Rules:

✅ Back to sleep, every time

✅ Firm, flat mattress

✅ Nothing soft in the crib

✅ Room share, not bed share

⚠️ Risk Factors:

🔹 Stomach or side sleeping

🔹 Overheating

🔹 Smoke exposure

🚨 Teaching:

✅ Supervised tummy time while awake

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Back to sleep, tummy to play!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #SafeSleep #Pediatrics #NewbornCare #PedsNursing #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client at 32 weeks of pregnancy asks about fetal kick counts. Which guideline should the nurse teach?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #320!

🤰 Baby's kicks tell a story. How many should mom feel?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 10 movements within 2 hours

🧠 Rationale: A common guideline is at least 10 fetal movements within 2 hours.

Count when the baby is usually active, often after a meal.

Fewer movements than usual should be reported right away.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Fetal Kick Counts

🤰 How to Count:

✅ Lie on the left side

✅ Count kicks, rolls and flutters

✅ Same time each day

⚠️ Report:

🔹 Fewer than 10 in 2 hours

🔹 A clear drop from the usual pattern

🚨 Next Steps:

🔹 Nonstress test may be ordered

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

TEN in TWO: ten kicks in two hours keeps worry away!

photos.question: A client says, "I just feel so overwhelmed today." Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #321!

🗣️ Therapeutic communication trips up so many students. Which one is right?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Tell me more about what you're feeling.

🧠 Rationale: An open-ended statement invites the client to share more.

"Why" questions can sound judgmental and make clients defensive.

False reassurance and "I know how you feel" shut the conversation down.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Therapeutic Communication

✅ Therapeutic:

🔹 Open-ended questions

🔹 Reflecting feelings

🔹 Silence and active listening

🔹 Clarifying

❌ Nontherapeutic:

🔹 "Why" questions

🔹 False reassurance

🔹 Giving advice

🔹 Changing the subject

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Keep it OPEN and about THEM: feelings first, fixes later!
